paper_title: The Unseen Targets of Hate -- A Systematic Review of Hateful   Communication Datasets
caption: : Linguistic and geographic trends over time in harmful language research. Notably, the number of datasets for the non-top five languages continues to be lower than all English ones, while since 2017 we see more and more datasets in languages other than English.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the number of datasets for various languages over time, from 2012 to 2022. The horizontal axis represents the year and contains 11 evenly spaced labels. The vertical axis represents the number of datasets, labeled as such, and has a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^2, with tick labels at 10^0, 10^1, and 10^2. The chart features grouped bars for six languages: English (blue), All other (orange), Arabic (green), Bengali (red), Spanish (purple), and Russian (brown). Each group of bars corresponds to a specific year, and the bars within each group represent the number of datasets for each language in that year. The English bars range from approximately 1 to 70, while the All other bars range from 0 to 60. The Arabic bars range from 0 to 20, the Bengali bars range from 0 to 10, the Spanish bars range from 0 to 20, and the Russian bars range from 0 to 10. The bars are not sorted in any specific order within each year, but the overall trend shows an increase in the number of datasets for most languages over time, with English consistently having one of the highest numbers. Notably, the chart does not have any visually emphasized bars, and there are no annotations or additional labels beyond the language legend.
